# SettlementOps

A finance-operations control centre for settlement reconciliation, built for the Razorpay
AI Buildathon (Track 4).

**Everything in this repository runs on synthetic data generated by this repository.** No
number here is a claim about Razorpay, about production systems, or about real money. See
[Limitations](#11-limitations).

> ### The headline result is negative for the AI, and it is stated up front
>
> The preregistered benchmark found that a **strong fixed workflow beat the AI agent
> decisively**: System B resolved 51.7% of the primary test split; the agent resolved
> **0.0%**. The AI resolution claim is killed by its own criteria. Full analysis in
> [`EVALUATION_REPORT.md`](EVALUATION_REPORT.md).
>
> That is not a footnote to work around. It is the point of running the experiment: this
> project uses **deterministic mechanisms for financial correctness** and treats AI as a
> bounded investigator whose every proposal passes a terminal verifier. The measurement
> says the deterministic half is carrying the system today, and the safety architecture
> held throughout — zero unsupported resolutions, zero `AMBIGUOUS` resolutions, every
> failure path landing on escalation.

---

## 1. The problem

A payment gateway settles thousands of payments a day. Most reconcile automatically: gross
minus fee minus tax equals what the bank credited, on the day the settlement calendar
predicted. A small residual does not, and someone has to work out why — was the fee
schedule different that week, did the settlement split across two UTRs, was a refund netted
into a later cycle, or is the variance genuinely unexplained?

That residual is expensive. It is also where mistakes are expensive: closing a case with
the wrong explanation moves money incorrectly.

## 2. The core idea

**The deterministic engine says where it stopped. The investigation says why.**

Reconciliation is a rules problem right up to the point where the rules run out. So this
system:

1. reconciles deterministically, and closes everything the rules can prove;
2. routes the residual to an investigation that gathers evidence through typed tools;
3. puts every proposed resolution through a **terminal deterministic verifier**;
4. hands the verified proposal to a **human**, who approves, rejects, or asks for more.

The AI never moves money, never closes a case, and never sees the verifier's answer.

## 3. Architecture

```
apps/api          Fastify edge. No business logic, no AI logic in a route.
apps/worker       Background jobs.
next-app/         Next.js operator UI (frozen; see UI_REDESIGN_REVIEW.md).

packages/domain          Money, policy, state machine, deterministic matcher. Zero deps.
packages/application     Use cases, ports, request context, authorization.
packages/persistence     PostgreSQL. The only package that knows SQL exists.
packages/tools           Typed, read-only, tenant-scoped evidence tools.
packages/agent           Ollama gateway, prompts, bounded investigation loop.
packages/verification    The terminal verifier.
packages/workflow        Investigation, AI dispatch, approval and staging.
packages/evaluation      Generator, systems A/B/C, scoring, hidden-truth store.
```

Dependency direction is enforced by `scripts/check-deps.ts`, which fails the build if the
domain imports a driver, or the agent imports persistence, or anything imports the
evaluation credential.

Money is `bigint` in integer minor units everywhere. `scripts/check-money-safety.ts` fails
the build on a float in a money path.

## 4. The deterministic baseline

`packages/domain/src/reconciliation/matcher.ts` runs ten independent checks — currency,
lifecycle order, duplicates, fee against the published schedule, settlement presence,
amount conservation, settlement timing, refund netting window, adjustment causality, bank
credit — and **fails closed**: any failed check produces an exception rather than a guess.

It is deliberately strong, and it must stay strong. Weakening it to flatter the AI would
invalidate the whole experiment, so it is frozen and pinned by tests.

## 5. The AI agent

Given a residual, the agent:

- reads the case (two opening tool calls are mandatory — an investigation that concludes
  before looking at the case is not an investigation);
- chooses which evidence to gather next, up to a budget of 8 tool calls and 8 steps;
- proposes one cause from a **closed taxonomy** and one disposition from a **closed set**,
  as schema-constrained JSON.

It cannot: run SQL, read files, call arbitrary HTTP, write anything, change a case state,
see hidden truth, or retry against the verifier. Tool arguments are validated; a tool name
that is not on the allowlist is rejected without the allowlist being echoed back.

Imported narration (an adjustment reference, for instance) is fenced as
`<untrusted_record_content>` and the system prompt says instructions inside it are to be
reported, not followed. The dataset contains adversarial cases carrying exactly such text,
so this is measured rather than asserted.

Every failure mode — model unavailable, timeout, malformed output, repeated tool call, no
progress, budget exhausted — lands on **escalation**. There is no path where a failure
produces a resolution.

## 6. The verifier

`packages/verification` is deterministic, pure, and **single-pass**. It checks evidence
provenance (every cited record must belong to the case), arithmetic, lifecycle possibility,
the cause/disposition policy table, and a per-cause support rule. A failed resolution is
**downgraded to escalation**, never returned to the model as feedback.

`AMBIGUOUS` can never resolve. That is definitional, not a threshold.

## 7. How it is evaluated

Three systems, same cases, same tools, same verifier:

| | What it is |
|---|---|
| **System A** | The deterministic baseline plus an enumerated reason-to-cause table |
| **System B** | A strong fixed workflow: all eight tools, always, in a documented order, with hand-written rules |
| **System C** | The bounded agent — chooses what to look at, composes the explanation |

System B exists to answer the question a reviewer should ask: *would more rules have done
just as well?* If it matches System C on unseen combinations, the AI contribution is killed
and the report says so.

**410 synthetic cases** across five merchant-disjoint splits, labelled by a frozen
combination registry rather than by hand:

| Split | Cases | Scored |
|---|---:|---|
| development | 120 | no — it defines what `SEEN` means |
| validation | 60 | no |
| showcase | 50 | **never** — so the demo cannot be accused of running on test data |
| primary test | 120 | yes |
| challenge | 60 | yes, reported separately |

Hidden truth lives in a **separate PostgreSQL database** with its own credential. The
application role has no `CONNECT` privilege on it; `tests/integration/eval-isolation.test.ts`
proves that in both directions.

A **leakage audit** runs before any benchmark and blocks it on failure. Probes are
cross-validated — an in-sample memoriser over 64 cells and 180 cases reports leakage that
is not there.

## 8. Running it locally

Prerequisites: Node 24+, pnpm 10, Docker, [Ollama](https://ollama.com).

> **Important: Ollama is required to run the AI investigation.**  
> The AI investigation engine connects to a local [Ollama](https://ollama.com) instance (default `http://127.0.0.1:11434` or configured via `OLLAMA_HOST`):
> - **Interactive Demo & UI investigations**: requires `qwen3:8b` (`ollama pull qwen3:8b`).
> - **Official benchmark reproduction**: requires `qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M` (`ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M`).
> 
> Ensure Ollama is running (`ollama serve`) before starting investigations. If Ollama is stopped or unreachable, the system fails closed gracefully: `/ready` reports `model: false`, and investigations are safely diverted to human escalation (`MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`) with zero financial mutation.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm db:up                                   # PostgreSQL on 5434
cp .env.example .env                         # then fill in the values below
pnpm db:migrate
```

`.env` for the application (note: `EVAL_DATABASE_URL` must NOT be here — the API refuses to
start if it is):

```
DATABASE_URL=postgres://settlementops_app:local_dev_only@localhost:5434/settlementops_app
MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=postgres://settlementops_migrator:local_dev_only@localhost:5434/settlementops_app
AUTH_ADAPTER=demo
API_PORT=3001
AI_INVESTIGATION_ENABLED=true
DEMO_SCENARIOS_ENABLED=true
OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3:8b
```

Pull the required model in Ollama:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3:8b                         # for demo / exploratory AI investigation
# or
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M       # for official frozen benchmark reproduction
```

Run the API and the UI:

```bash
pnpm --filter @settlementops/api start       # http://localhost:3000
cd next-app && pnpm dev                      # http://localhost:3001
```

Check it is up:

```bash
curl localhost:3000/health    # liveness  - does no I/O
curl localhost:3000/ready     # readiness - checks database, and the model when AI is on
curl localhost:3000/metrics   # operational counters
```

### Production-like stack

```bash
export POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...            # required; there is no default
export DATABASE_URL=...                 # application role
export MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=...       # migrator role, used once at startup
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
```

API, worker and PostgreSQL, with health checks, an ordered migration gate, a persistent
volume and a non-root user. Ollama is **not** containerised: it is a large stateful runtime
with its own model store and, usually, GPU access, so it is treated as an external
dependency and pointed at with `OLLAMA_HOST`.

With `NODE_ENV=production` the process **refuses to start** if `AUTH_ADAPTER=demo`, if demo
scenarios are enabled, or if the evaluation credential is present in its environment. Those
are startup failures, not warnings.

## 9. Reproducing the benchmark

The evaluation uses its own database and credential.

```bash
export EVAL_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=postgres://settlementops_migrator:local_dev_only@localhost:5434/settlementops_eval
export EVAL_DATABASE_URL=postgres://settlementops_eval:local_dev_only_eval@localhost:5434/settlementops_eval

pnpm eval:db:migrate     # create the hidden-truth schema
pnpm eval:leakage        # must PASS before anything is generated or scored
pnpm eval:generate       # 410 cases through the real import + reconciliation path
pnpm eval:run            # A, B and C over the scored splits -> eval-results.json
```

`pnpm eval:run -- --systems=A,B` skips the model. `--limit=20` is a smoke run.

The **exploratory** agent variants (`AGENT_PROMPT_VARIANT=v2`, `AGENT_LOOP_VARIANT=v2`) are
refused on any scored split by the runner itself. They may run on validation, development or
showcase only, and their numbers are never preregistered.

The model is pinned by **digest**, not tag — Ollama tags are mutable. `eval:run` refuses to
run System C if the installed digest does not match the manifest.

## 10. The demo path

```
Create scenario -> import -> deterministic reconciliation -> residual exception
  -> operator opens the case
  -> investigation: agent chooses evidence, tools return it
  -> agent proposes a cause and disposition
  -> verifier accepts or downgrades
  -> human approves / rejects / requests evidence
  -> staged as an intent; audit trail shows every step
```

A second case demonstrates safe abstention: the evidence is genuinely ambiguous, and the
system escalates rather than choosing.

## 11. Limitations

- **All data is synthetic**, generated by `packages/evaluation`. Every number measures this
  system against our own generator and our own oracle on 410 constructed cases. It says
  nothing about real merchant data, real volume, or real distribution shift.
- **The model is small.** `qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M` was chosen because the evaluation
  host is CPU-only with 15.4 GB of RAM; a 7B build runs at roughly a third of the
  throughput, which would have put a 180-case scored run out of reach. This is a ceiling on
  the RESULT, not on the architecture.
- **120 primary-test cases** support an aggregate comparison, not per-cause point
  estimates. Per-cause numbers are descriptive and are reported with their intervals.
- **No holiday calendar** in the settlement model; business days are Mon–Fri.
- **Single currency** (INR). FX is out of scope.
- Most financial constants are **synthetic assumptions**, documented as such in
  `D7_FINALIZATION_REVIEW.md`. Only the CARD fee rate (250 bps) and GST on fee (1800 bps)
  are derived from the specification's own worked example.
- **Staging is where the system stops.** Nothing writes to a ledger, and there is no code
  path that would.
